# Hand-labeled V1 fixtures

positions.json labels exact tactical/material facts and documented phase rules,
with a reason for each expected value. The labels were not generated by the extractor.
Development PGN: both players castle (White move 4, Black move 5); Nf3 and Nc3
are different knights, Ng5 repeats the g1 knight; Qe2 is early by the move-10 rule.
First White elapsed is 2 seconds, Black 4 seconds under 600+5; White's next EMT
is explicitly 2 seconds. Missing clocks break the own-player clock chain.
Additional clock/context/error scenarios live as explicit parameterized unit cases.
PGN results declare completion (resignation is allowed); these are synthetic fixtures.

Historical fixtures are anonymized copies of completed PGN declarations from the
existing Phase 10 corpus (IDs 3, 10, 20). Only White/Black labels and retained
Result/TimeControl headers are used; moves and timing comments are preserved.
Independent selected-position inspection, using board piece counts:

- Tactical, 14 plies: 4...Qa5+ checks; 6.Bxb5 captures a queen (+9); 6...cxb5
  immediately recaptures the bishop (+3 for Black). All positions remain opening.
- Middle, 80 plies: White castles at ply 7, Black at 18; last move Re1# mates.
  Before that move there are two rooks, one bishop, one knight (16 non-pawn
  points), hence middlegame despite no queens.
- Endgame, 139 plies: before ply 52 (Rxh4), two rooks and two knights total 16;
  before ply 53 (Nd7+), two rooks and one knight total 13. Endgame starts at
  ply 53 and persists through the final Qc1#.
